user.title: Connect to a SPIFFE Workload API
user.description: Home Assistant gets its SPIFFE identity from a Workload API served on a Unix socket, for example by an agent running as an app (add-on). Any SPIFFE implementation works.

data_description.socket: A unix:// address as Home Assistant sees it, such as unix:///config/.spiffe/agent.sock
A unix:// address as Home Assistant sees it, such as unix:///config/.spiffe/agent.sock

error.invalid_socket: This is not a valid address. Use unix:///absolute/path/to/agent.sock.
error.socket_missing: There is no socket at this path yet. Start the agent first, then try again.
error.cannot_connect: The socket exists but the Workload API did not answer. Check that the agent is running and can reach its issuer.
error.no_identity: The Workload API answers, but has no identity for Home Assistant. Register (admit) Home Assistant with your SPIFFE implementation, then try again.

abort.reconfigure_successful: The Workload API address was changed.

workload_api_unreachable.title: The SPIFFE Workload API is not answering
workload_api_unreachable.description:
For more than five minutes, Home Assistant could not reach the Workload API at {socket}. Integrations that use SPIFFE cannot get tokens until it answers again.

Check that the agent is running. The last error was: {error}

permission_denied.title: Home Assistant was refused a SPIFFE token
permission_denied.description:
An integration asked for a JWT-SVID, and the Workload API refused it. Usually Home Assistant has not been admitted (registered) at the issuer yet, or the issuer does not allow the audience that was requested.

The error was: {error}

no_identity.title: The SPIFFE Workload API has no identity for Home Assistant
no_identity.description:
The Workload API answers, but refuses to give Home Assistant anything, not even the trust bundles. Usually Home Assistant has not been registered (admitted) with your SPIFFE implementation yet. Home Assistant keeps retrying.

The error was: {error}

init.title: Home Assistant's SPIFFE identity
init.description: Set Home Assistant's own SPIFFE ID to let other workloads call it with a JWT-SVID. It is the audience every incoming token must name. While it is empty, incoming requests are answered with 503.

data_description.spiffe_id: For example spiffe://example.org/ha/core. Leave empty to not accept incoming requests.
data_description.expose_whoami: Lets a workload POST its token to /api/spiffe/whoami and be told who Home Assistant sees. Handy for checking a setup, off by default.
data_description.single_use_tokens: Refuse a token that was already accepted. Only enable this if your SPIFFE issuer mints a fresh token for every fetch; agents that cache tokens, such as SPIRE and spiffex, will have repeated calls refused.

error.invalid_spiffe_id: This is not a valid SPIFFE ID. Use spiffe://trust-domain/path.

user.title: Add an event webhook
user.description: A webhook that only answers workloads presenting a JWT-SVID from one of the allowed callers. Each verified request fires a spiffe_webhook event.

data_description.name: Shown in the event data.
data_description.webhook_id: Part of the URL, /api/webhook/<ID>. A random one is suggested.
data_description.allowed_callers: The SPIFFE IDs that may call it, for example spiffe://example.org/orders/api. At least one.

data_description.name: Shown in the event data.
data_description.allowed_callers: The SPIFFE IDs that may call it. At least one.

error.name_in_use: Another event webhook already has this name.
error.invalid_webhook_id: Use 8 to 128 letters, digits, dashes or underscores.
error.webhook_id_in_use: Another event webhook already uses this ID.
error.invalid_spiffe_id: One of the callers is not a valid SPIFFE ID. Use spiffe://trust-domain/path.

http_request.name: HTTP request with a JWT-SVID
http_request.description: Calls a URL with Home Assistant's identity as a bearer token for the audience you name. Administrators only, because the token goes to whatever server the URL points at.

audience.name: Audience
audience.description: The SPIFFE ID of the service you are calling, such as spiffe://example.org/orders/api.

json.name: JSON body
json.description: An object to send as the JSON body.

headers.name: Headers
headers.description: Extra headers. Authorization cannot be set.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the whole request.

invalid_url.message: The URL must be an http or https URL.

authorization_header.message: The Authorization header is set by this action and cannot be overridden.

invalid_header.message: The header {header} is not valid. Names must be plain header tokens, and values cannot contain line breaks or null characters.
